chunks: And 'Abdullah ibn al-Qasim narrated from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I said to Abu 'Abdullah (peace be upon him)
I buy the female slave from a trustworthy man, and he informed me that he had not touched her since she had her menstruation at his place and had become pure at his place.
He said: 'It is not permissible for you to have intercourse with her until you have verified her purity with one menstruation, but what is below the private part is permissible.
Indeed, those who buy female slaves and then have intercourse with them before verifying their purity, those are fornicators with their wealth.'

key_terms.مَا دُونَ الْفَرْجِ: What is below the private part (sexual organs)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on having intercourse with a newly purchased female slave if the seller claims she is a virgin?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in the chapter on *Milk al-Yaman* (ownership of the right hand), where Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that even if the seller is trustworthy, the buyer must ensure the slave woman has completed one full menstrual cycle (*istibra*) to confirm she is not pregnant. The Imam distinguishes between permissible non-genital intimacy and full intercourse, warning that premature consummation without this verification constitutes *zawaj al-mal* (marriage with wealth), a concept linking the financial transaction to the sexual act.
